<think>
7 x 8 is 7 x 7 plus one more 7, so 49 + 7 = 56.
</think>

56.
are you sure? I always mix that one up

<think>
It is a common pair to confuse, so worth confirming from a different anchor.
</think>

<think>
Starting from 8 x 8 = 64 and removing one 8 gives 64 - 8 = 56. Going the other way, 7 x 10 = 70, and subtracting 7 x 2 = 14 leaves 56. Two different starting points, same destination.
</think>

56. Confirmed two ways: 8 x 8 minus 8 gives 56, and 7 x 10 minus 14 gives 56.
how do you know that is right?

<think>
Good to confirm since division errors are easy to make.
</think>

<think>
Multiplying back: 12 x 12 = 144, which recovers the original number. Another way, 144 is 12 squared, so the square root of 144 is 12, and dividing a number by itself gives 1, so 144 / 12 = 12.
</think>

12. Confirmed by multiplying 12 x 12 = 144 and by recognising 144 as 12 squared.
